bull_bear.body:
- Promoter and employee industry experience in the foam business since inception
- In-house, technology-driven manufacturing facility (ISO 9001:2015, BIS IS 7933:2022) with QR-code product traceability and warranty registration
- Extensive pan-India sales and distribution network spanning 13 states with 1,300+ dealers
- Long-standing dealer relationships despite no long-term contractual agreements
- Focus on quality control and timely delivery
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- No long-term dealer/customer contracts — Company generally does not enter into long-term agreements with its ~1,300 dealers/customers, so relationships (and revenue) rest on continuity of goodwill rather than contractual commitment
- State-level revenue concentration — Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Delhi together accounted for ~71% of FY25 revenue from operations, with Punjab alone at 27.37%
- Single-site manufacturing concentration — All PU Foam production runs from one facility in Ambala, Haryana (15,000 TPA); any disruption there affects the whole business
- Imported raw-material dependence — Key inputs TDI and polyols are sourced from overseas suppliers in Hong Kong, Thailand and Singapore at monthly-reset prices, exposing margins to forex and import-price volatility
- Related-party transaction exposure — Recurring sales, borrowings, remuneration and rent transactions with promoter-owned/-interested entities (Aggarwal Comforts, Charming Fashions, Omesha Infraprojects LLP, Sukh Sampada Builders LLP) create potential conflict-of-interest exposure
- Volatile revenue growth — Revenue from operations growth swung from +13.33% (FY23) to -7.63% (FY24) to +10.06% (FY25), indicating limited growth predictability
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Full-stack vertically integrated manufacturer: sources principal raw materials (TDI, polyols, catalysts, additives) from local and overseas (Hong Kong, Thailand, Singapore) suppliers at monthly-reset prices with 50-70 day supplier credit; manufactures PU Foam in-house via a continuous foaming line (raw-material mixing, foam forming/settling, curing for at least 12 hours, cutting) at its own facility; combines cut foam with spring/rubberised coir and processes into finished mattresses/cushions in-house; certain finished products such as pillows are outsourced on a job-work basis to third-party manufacturers; distributes exclusively through a pan-India dealer network (no owned retail stores) and also sells PU Foam grades directly to third-party manufacturers of furniture, sports products, seat covers, shoes and apparel.

market_position.basis: Per the DRHP's own peer-comparison table, Sham Foam Limited's FY25 revenue from operations of Rs. 8,114.82 lakhs is a small fraction of listed peers Sheela Foam Limited (Rs. 2,58,750.00 lakhs) and Wakefit Innovations Ltd (Rs. 1,27,369.10 lakhs), indicating a small-scale, regionally concentrated position relative to organised industry peers.

opportunities: White-space opportunity in Tier-II and Tier-III cities where organized retail penetration remains limited
Emerging segments such as smart mattresses and subscription models create differentiation pathways for innovative players
threats: Environmental Concerns and Regulations - PU foam production faces scrutiny regarding volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions and recyclability challenges; stricter environmental regulations in North America and Europe are increasing compliance costs for manufacturers
Consumer Perceptions of Quality - some buyers still associate poly-foam mattresses with lower quality compared to latex
Direct-to-consumer brands offering 25-50% lower prices than traditional players are forcing established manufacturers to recalibrate pricing strategies and invest in digital capabilities

Industry shows moderate fragmentation with the top five companies (including Sheela Foam/Sleepwell and Kurlon) estimated to command a major market share in 2024, while start-ups like Wakefit and The Sleep Company gain rapid traction through backward integration and data-driven marketing

internal_operational.detail: The sole registered office cum manufacturing facility is on leased premises; inability to renew on commercially suitable terms or relocate could materially disrupt operations.
internal_operational.evidence: 2,04,460 sq. ft. leased from Rajinder Kumar Jindal, Sanjeev Kumar Jindal and Monica Jindal for 30 years w.e.f. 1st August, 2025 to 31st July, 2055
internal_operational.title: Leased registered office cum manufacturing facility

internal_operational.detail: Revenue is significantly dependent on a limited number of customers with no long-term agreements; loss of key customers would adversely affect operations.
internal_operational.evidence: Top 10 customers contributed 25.51% (FY23), 28.02% (FY24), 26.83% (FY25) and 25.10% (H1FY26) of revenue from operations
internal_operational.title: Customer concentration

internal_operational.detail: No long-term agreements with raw-material suppliers; volatility in supply/pricing of diisocyanates, polyols and additives could hamper production.
internal_operational.evidence: Cost of materials consumed was Rs. 3,008.96 lakhs (79.46% of revenue) for H1FY26; top 10 suppliers accounted for 88.34% (H1FY26), 78.31% (FY25), 86.85% (FY24), 88.07% (FY23) of purchases
internal_operational.title: Raw material supply/pricing volatility, no formal supplier contracts

internal_operational.detail: Manufacturing is concentrated in Haryana and revenue is concentrated in a handful of northern Indian states, exposing the company to regional disruptions.
internal_operational.evidence: Punjab 21.53%, Uttar Pradesh 23.52%, Haryana 13.47%, Delhi 10.95% of H1FY26 revenue from operations; single manufacturing facility in Ambala, Haryana
internal_operational.title: Geographic concentration of operations and revenue

internal_operational.detail: Business is dependent on one manufacturing facility; any shutdown (power interruption, equipment breakdown, natural disaster) could adversely affect operations.
internal_operational.evidence: Single facility at Khasra No. 18/16/2, Ambala, Haryana; backup DG set for power interruptions; no past instances of shutdown disclosed
internal_operational.title: Dependence on single Manufacturing Facility

internal_operational.detail: Handling of raw materials in insulated tanks and mixing equipment could lead to accidents causing injury, property damage or civil/criminal liability.
internal_operational.evidence: No material incident requiring insurance claim in the past three financial years, per the Company

strategy_growth.detail: The home comfort products and PU Foam industry in India is competitive and fragmented, with organised and unorganised competitors, some larger with more resources.
strategy_growth.evidence: Qualitative; low barriers to entry in mattress/upholstery segment cited
strategy_growth.title: Competitive and fragmented industry

strategy_growth.detail: Failure to anticipate shifts in consumer preference (e.g., toward spring/coir vs. foam) or industry trends in customer sectors (automotive, garments, footwear) could reduce demand.
strategy_growth.title: Changing consumer preferences and industry trends

strategy_growth.detail: Business success heavily depends on continued services of Promoters (particularly Rajinder Kumar Jindal and Sanjeev Kumar Jindal) and KMP/SMP; loss of key personnel could impair growth and operations.
strategy_growth.title: Dependence on Promoters, KMP and Senior Management

strategy_growth.detail: Expansion into new geographic markets carries risks including unfamiliarity with local conditions, staffing difficulties and lack of reputation.
strategy_growth.title: Risk of unsuccessful geographic expansion

strategy_growth.detail: Failure to maintain/enhance brand and reputation could reduce client trust and adversely affect the business.
strategy_growth.title: Brand and reputation risk

strategy_growth.detail: Negative publicity related to the Company, brand or products could erode reputation and results of operations.
strategy_growth.title: Negative publicity risk

concerns_observed: 100% of the Rs. 1,371.65 lakhs Net-Proceeds capex (civil construction plus machinery from M/s A S Enterprises and M/s. Suresh Kumar Jindal Contractor) rests only on vendor quotations; no orders have been placed and the objects are not appraised by any bank or financial institution.

PU Foam capacity utilization at the Ambala facility fell to 38% in H1FY26 (not annualised) from 80% in FY25, 78% in FY24 and 81% in FY23, on an unchanged installed capacity of 15,000 TPA, even as the Issue funds capacity-adding machinery at the same site.

Debtor days rose from 58 (FY23) to 225 (H1FY26); trade receivables reached Rs. 2,471.42 lakhs, 65.26% of H1FY26 revenue, versus 26.99% of revenue in FY25; the working-capital gap widened to Rs. 1,847.87 lakhs in H1FY26 from Rs. 1,533.20 lakhs in FY23.

No long-term agreements exist with customers, suppliers or dealers: top-10 customers were 25.10-28.02% of revenue and top-10 suppliers 78.31-88.34% of purchases across FY23-H1FY26, run through a 1,300+-dealer network with no formal dealer agreements.

Outstanding litigation totals Rs. 726.63 lakhs (227.51% of PAT and 46.41% of networth): by/against the Company Rs. 26.50 lakhs / Rs. 200.13 lakhs, and by/against the Promoters Rs. 280.00 lakhs / Rs. 220.00 lakhs.

Unsecured related-party loans of Rs. 643.75 lakhs outstanding as on 30 September 2025, sourced from Promoters, Promoter Group members and entities such as Charming Fashions Private Limited and Aggarwal Comforts Private Limited, carry 0% interest and are repayable on demand.

History of delayed statutory compliance: 19 delayed RoC e-form filings from FY2020-21 to FY2025-26 (MGT-14, PAS-3, CHG-1, ADT-1, DPT-3, INC-27, AOC-4, DIR-12), plus EPF delays of 16 and 4 days, ESIC delays of 4 and 3 days, and TDS return delays of 10, 48 and 64 days.

The entire product range is produced at one leased facility in Ambala, and revenue is concentrated in four states as of H1FY26 - Punjab (21.53%), Uttar Pradesh (23.52%), Haryana (13.47%) and Delhi (10.95%), together about 69% of revenue.
data_gaps: Issue Price, dilution percentage and post-Issue Promoter holding are all marked '[●]' in the extracted document; Bankers to the Issue, Refund Bank and Sponsor Bank are also undisclosed.

Promoter pre-issue holding is recorded as 80.27% in the shareholding-pattern summary field, but the individually listed 1%+ Promoter/Promoter-Group shareholders (Rajinder Kumar Jindal, Sanjeev Kumar Jindal, Abhinav Jindal, Deepika Jindal, Kunal Jindal, Monica Jindal, Charming Fashion Private Limited) sum to approximately 99.99% - the two figures are inconsistent in the source extraction.

The Company states no contingent liability exists for H1FY26, FY25, FY24 or FY23, but the accompanying summary table in the extracted source carries figures of Rs. 200.10 lakhs and Rs. 2.50 lakhs whose period-mapping is unclear due to table-extraction artifacts.
Employee headcount is not disclosed (count, as-of date and note are all blank or null in the extracted data).

Outcome of the 5 pending trademark assignment applications (nos. 4628207, 4628025, 4628230, 1919784, 4628006) and the device-mark application no. 6551281 (filed 30 July 2024), both still under process.
verdict.our_read: Sham Foam is a single-facility (Ambala, Haryana) PU foam and mattress manufacturer whose FY23-H1FY26 revenue is 84.69-93.08% dependent on PU Foam sold through a 1,300+-dealer network, raising Rs. 1,371.65 lakhs of capex for which 100% of orders remain unplaced even as H1FY26 capacity utilization fell to 38% (not annualised) and debtor days rose to 225.
post_listing_commitments: Capex of up to Rs. 1,371.65 lakhs (civil construction Rs. 312.39 lakhs plus machinery Rs. 1,106.91 lakhs) to be deployed in FY2026-27, funded entirely from Net Proceeds.
Working capital of up to Rs. 1,425.00 lakhs to be deployed in two tranches - up to Rs. 825.00 lakhs in FY2026-27 and up to Rs. 600.00 lakhs in FY2027-28.
General Corporate Purposes capped at the lower of 15% of Gross Proceeds or Rs. 1,000.00 lakhs (Rs. 10 crore).
red_flags: Promoter Group entity Aggarwal Comfort Products Private Limited operates in a business similar to the Company's, with no non-compete agreement disclosed.

Key brand names DECORWELL and FEATHERFRESH are registered as trademarks in the personal names of Promoter Sanjeev Kumar Jindal and Promoter Group member Parwati Devi rather than the Company, used under a Resource Sharing Agreement pending assignment via 5 applications dated 10-11 March 2026.

Individual Promoters' average cost of acquisition is Rs. 0.22/share (Rajinder Kumar Jindal, Sanjeev Kumar Jindal, Monica Jindal, Deepika Jindal) and Rs. 11.11/share for Charming Fashion Private Limited, against an undisclosed Issue Price; a 1:50 bonus issue of 1,64,250 shares was allotted to Promoters/Promoter Group on 5 July 2025, within one year of this Draft Prospectus.
strengths_observed: EBITDA margin expanded from 1.68% (FY23) to 6.01% (FY24), 5.78% (FY25) and 10.74% (H1FY26); PAT margin rose from 0.87% to 8.43% over the same span, with RONW of 40.79%/33.40%/28.74%/20.40% respectively.
Total debt fell from Rs. 1,840.20 lakhs (FY23) to Rs. 921.61 lakhs (FY25) and Rs. 711.95 lakhs (H1FY26), while networth grew from Rs. 170.78 lakhs to Rs. 1,565.75 lakhs over the same period.
No shares held by Promoters are pledged or otherwise encumbered, and the DRHP discloses no defaults or rescheduling of borrowings.
The Ambala facility holds ISO 9001:2015 and BIS Certification No. IS 7933:2022, and its lease was renewed for a 30-year term running 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2055.
Pre-issue capital structure is uncomplicated: only 7 shareholders as of the Draft Prospectus date, no ESOP/ESPS shares ever issued, and no outstanding convertible instruments, warrants or DVRs.
